sections.title: The Apostles' Boldness and Miraculous Signs
observations: The early church experienced a powerful outpouring of the Holy Spirit, leading to miraculous signs and wonders performed by the apostles. This boldness in preaching the gospel was a direct result of their reliance on the Holy Spirit.
The unity and communal living of the believers is highlighted, showcasing their commitment to one another and the mission of the church.

sections.title: Ananias and Sapphira
observations: The story of Ananias and Sapphira serves as a sobering reminder of the seriousness of sin within the church. Their deceit in lying about their offering demonstrates the importance of integrity and honesty in the body of Christ.
This incident also illustrates the concept of divine judgment and the fear of the Lord that should permeate the church community.

sections.title: The Apostles Persecuted
observations: The apostles faced persecution for their faith, which is a recurring theme in the book of Acts. Their response to persecution was to continue preaching boldly, demonstrating their commitment to the mission of Christ.
The angelic intervention that freed them from prison emphasizes God's sovereignty and support for His servants in the face of opposition.

importantVerses.commentary: Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit? This verse highlights the seriousness of lying to God and the influence of Satan in the lives of believers.
We must obey God rather than men. This declaration by Peter underscores the priority of obedience to God over human authority, a key principle for believers.

questions: What does the story of Ananias and Sapphira teach us about the nature of sin and accountability in the church?
How can we apply the apostles' boldness in the face of persecution to our own lives today?
What does it mean to obey God rather than men in our current cultural context?
